_extraction_flags.notes: Valid Fiber-ISAC paper! DNN-based DBP enables dual-function: nonlinear compensation for comm + power profile estimation / anomaly detection for sensing.

reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Fig.1: DNN-based DBP architecture with training/sensing branches. Fig.2: 15×80 km SSMF link. Fig.3: BER vs launch power (communication), γ* profile (sensing). Fig.4: Anomaly detection at 360km, 760km.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: System: Double-effect DNN-based DBP for Fiber-ISAC. The optimized γ* (nonlinear parameter) serves dual purpose: (1) nonlinear compensation for communication, (2) power distribution estimation and anomaly detection for sensing. Uses training sequence - no additional bandwidth overhead.
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Comm: 28 GBaud 16-QAM, 1200 km (15×80 km). BER ~1e-5 at optimal launch power. Sensing: γ* profile shows EDFA positions, detects 1-5 dB losses at 360/760 km. 20 km step size for fine resolution.
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: Contribution: First DNN-based DBP for ISAC. Dual-use of trained parameters. No additional hardware/bandwidth. Gap: Sensing resolution limited when multiple anomalies in same span.

bibliographic.title: Double-effect DNN-based DBP Scheme for Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC)
bibliographic.authors: Feiyu Li, Xian Zhou, Qirui Fan, Yuyuan Gao, Jiahao Huo, Jinhui Yuan, Keping Long

application.scenario_description: Long-haul coherent optical transmission with simultaneous link status monitoring for power profile estimation and anomaly detection.

enabling_tech.ml_details: DNN-based Digital Back-Propagation (DBP) with supervised training. Adam optimizer, 15000 training symbols, 50 iterations.

key_contribution.key_contribution: DNN-based DBP enables dual-function: nonlinear compensation (communication) and power profile / anomaly detection (sensing) using the same optimized γ* parameters.
key_contribution.gap_addressed: Previous DBP and sensing methods were separate. This integrates them without additional bandwidth or hardware.

transmitter.notes: 28 GBaud 16-QAM coherent system. RRC filter (roll-off 0.18). Laser linewidth 100 kHz.

receiver.notes: Coherent receiver with DSP: CD comp, SP-LMS, FOE, CPR (BPS), DNN-based DBP.

integration.notes: DSP-level integration. Same trained parameters serve both comm (nonlinear comp) and sensing (anomaly detection).

waveform.notes: Standard 16-QAM signal. Sensing derived from trained nonlinear parameters γ*. No separate sensing waveform.

channel_wireless.notes: 15×80 km SSMF (1200 km total). α=0.2 dB/km, D=17 ps/nm/km, γ=1.3 W⁻¹km⁻¹. EDFA per span (NF=6 dB).

comm_metrics.notes: 28 GBaud × 4 bits/symbol = 112 Gbps (single pol). BER ~1e-5 at optimal launch power with 20 km step DBP.

sensing_metrics.notes: 20 km step size for γ* profile. Detects 1-5 dB anomalous losses. Locates EDFA positions. Limited when multiple anomalies in same 80 km span.

tradeoff.notes: Smaller DBP step improves both BER and sensing resolution. 20 km step: better BER + finer loss localization.
